ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the isosceles right-angled $\triangle ABC$, where $AC=BC$ and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, point D is a moving point on side $AC$ (not coinciding with A or C). A line is drawn from point A perpendicular to $BD$ at point E, and $AE$ is extended to intersect the extension of $BC$ at point F. $CE$ is connected. Then, what is the measure of $\angle BEC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw $CH \perp AF$ at $H$, and $CG \perp BE$ at $G$,\\
$\therefore \angle AHC=\angle BGC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$, and $AF\perp BE$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEB=\angle BCD=\angle BEF=90^\circ$,\\
Also, since $\angle ADE=\angle BDC$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAH=\angle CBG$,\\
Also, since $AC=BC$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AHC\cong \triangle BCG$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore CH=CG$,\\
Since $CH\perp EF$, and $CG\perp BE$,\\
$\therefore CE$ bisects $\angle BEF$,\\
$\therefore \angle BEC= \frac{1}{2}\angle BEF=\boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows right triangle ABC with C at the right angle, AC drawn vertically and BC horizontally, and AC = BC. Point D is on segment AC. The line through B and D also passes through E, and the line through A and E continues to F on the extension of BC. Segment CE is drawn. Reasoning following the assigned method: From the construction, AE is perpendicular to BD at E. Since B, E, and D are collinear, this gives AE ⟂ EB, so ∠AEB = 90°. Also, the triangle has ∠ACB = 90°. Therefore both C and E see segment AB under a right angle, so A, C, E, and B lie on the same circle with diameter AB. In this circle, ∠BEC and ∠BAC are inscribed angles subtending the same chord BC; from the diagram A and E are on the same side of BC, so these angles are equal. Since triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle with AC = BC and right angle at C, the acute angles are equal, hence ∠BAC = 45°. Therefore ∠BEC = 45°.
